title: UK and Canada Visa Changes Reshape Choices for Indian Students
excerpt: The UK cuts post-study work to 18 months for Graduate applications from January 2027, while Canada caps permits and raises required living funds to CAD 23,448.
body:
• UK Graduate visa: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027; PhD graduates keep 3 years.
  • UK Student visa maintenance is £1,529 a month in London and £1,171 a month outside London, for up to 9 months, held for 28 days; the visa fee from outside the UK is £558.
  • Canada: a single study-permit applicant outside Quebec must show CAD 23,448 for living expenses from 1 September 2026, plus tuition and travel.
  • Reader action: check your application date against those cutoffs before you file — the date you apply, not the date you start, decides which UK Graduate duration and which Canada funds threshold applies to you.

For Indian students choosing between the United Kingdom and Canada, the decision is now shaped less by university rankings and more by visa arithmetic: how long you can work after graduation, how much money you must show before you leave, and how tightly each country is capping new arrivals. Both countries have tightened their student routes over the past two years, and the changes are already showing up in application numbers.

The UK: a shorter post-study window

The clearest change is the Graduate route. According to GOV.UK, a Graduate visa lasts 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026 and 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027. Doctoral graduates keep 3 years. The visa costs £937 plus the healthcare surcharge, usually £1,035 for each year in the UK, and you must apply from inside the UK before your Student visa expires, after your university tells the Home Office you have completed your course.

Entry has also become more expensive and more restricted. The GOV.UK Student visa page lists a £558 application fee from outside the UK and a maintenance requirement of £1,529 a month for courses in London and £1,171 a month elsewhere, for up to 9 months, with the money held for at least 28 days. Dependants are now limited to specific categories, principally research postgraduates and government-sponsored students, so most taught master’s students can no longer bring family.

The effect on demand has been sharp. Reporting summarised by Connect My India said Indian study visas to the UK fell from 159,371 in 2023 to about 92,355 in 2024, before a modest rebound to around 98,000 in the year ending June 2025, as dependent restrictions and higher financial thresholds took effect.

"Applications submitted before January 1, 2027, will continue under current terms, while later cohorts will move to an 18-month post-study work period."

— Mayank Maheshwari, co-founder, University Living, via Connect My India

Canada: caps, higher funds and higher refusals

Canada has moved from open growth to controlled intake. Caps introduced in 2024 limited new study permits to approximately 360,000 nationwide, alongside provincial attestation requirements and tighter screening. The same reporting put refusal rates for Indian applicants at around 74% by August 2025, compared with about 32% in August 2023.

The financial bar rose again this autumn. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada’s updated amounts, reported by Passage from IRCC’s official page, require a single applicant outside Quebec applying on or after 1 September 2026 to show CAD 23,448 for living expenses, up from CAD 22,895. That figure is for living costs only — tuition for the first year and transportation to and from Canada must be shown in addition, and applicants on longer programmes must explain how they will fund the full duration.

What this means for Indian applicants

Put together, the two systems reward earlier, better-documented applications. A student finishing a UK course in late 2026 who files for the Graduate visa before 31 December keeps a full two years to find sponsored work; filing a week later costs six months. A Canada applicant filing after 1 September 2026 needs the higher funds figure, with four to six months of bank history rather than a last-minute deposit. Consultants quoted in the reporting say both countries are now favouring candidates with strong academic records, sufficient financial backing and skills aligned with labour-market needs, rather than applicants treating study primarily as a migration pathway.

Families should also price the alternatives honestly. Germany, Ireland and other destinations are drawing more Indian interest as the traditional routes narrow, but the UK and Canada remain large, English-language systems with deep Indian student communities — provided applicants plan around the new dates and thresholds instead of discovering them at filing.

What to do next

Before applying, confirm the live figures on GOV.UK’s Graduate visa page and on IRCC’s proof-of-financial-support page via Canada.ca, and keep the application-date rules in front of you: 31 December 2026 for the UK Graduate duration, and 1 September 2026 for Canada’s CAD 23,448 threshold.
